newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares fall prey to profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares fall prey to profit-taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares tumbled 5.68 percent on meagre turnover on Wednesday on what traders said was natural profit-taking after recent sharp and rapid gains.
Today's fall was seen as a long-overdue correction, and with sentiment still bouyant, market seen headed for long-term growth, traders said.

The SBI index fell 92.15 points to 1,530.6. The blue-chip index fell for the first time after 13 consecutive days' of gains. The index is up 32.4 percent since the beginning of 1997, driven higher by strong demand from foreign investors.

"This was just a correction, which should not last too long -- growth has just begun and I expect prices to continue rising over the next six months supported by foreign buying," Franci Zmavc, a trader at brokerage Intara said.
Market turnover fell to 413.7 million tolars from 990.9 million tolars. Overall 13 shares fell, six rose and six were untraded.

"Beside Slovenian food processing and pharmaceutical companies, foreign investors are also interested in investing into banks," Fritz Schweiger, head of equity research at Investmentbank Austria in Vienna said.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 2.08 percent to 58,750 tolars on volume 2,547 shares for total turnover of 148.5 million tolars.
Demand for SKB bank has burgeoned due to the bank's plan to list global depository receipts on the London stock exchange by mid-February.
Financial consultancy Primofin led the day's decliners, falling 7.93 percent to 13,810 tolars on volume of 17 shares.
Construction company GPG was by far the biggest gainer, jumping 9.50 percent to 8,760 tolars on volume of 735 shares.
